---
title: "The Sensor Zoo"
subtitle: "Vetted specifications for the cameras, LiDARs, IMUs, and safety scanners used in the physical AI examples"
---

The Sensor Zoo lists every sensor in the `mlsysim.Sensors` registry. Each entry carries units and a
provenance record, so the timing and bandwidth numbers that feed information-age and ingestion
budgets trace back to a datasheet.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to use this page
Use these sensors to budget the time between an event and the moment the system can act on it: exposure, readout, transport, and processing. Load any sensor directly in Python, for example
`camera = mlsysim.Sensors.Camera.Sony_IMX477`.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sys
from pathlib import Path

for candidate in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]:
    pkg_dir = candidate / "mlsysim"
    if (pkg_dir / "mlsysim" / "__init__.py").exists():
        if str(pkg_dir) not in sys.path:
            sys.path.insert(0, str(pkg_dir))
        break

import mlsysim
from mlsysim import Sensors


def q(value, unit=None, precision=1):
    if value is None:
        return "---"
    if unit is not None:
        value = value.to(unit)
    return f"{value.magnitude:,.{precision}f} {value.units:~P}"


def entries(namespace):
    for attr in sorted(dir(namespace)):
        if attr.startswith("_"):
            continue
        item = getattr(namespace, attr)
        if hasattr(item, "name") and hasattr(item, "nominal_latency"):
            yield attr, item


cameras = list(entries(Sensors.Camera))
print("### Cameras\n")
print("| Sensor | Resolution | Frame rate | Shutter | Exposure | Readout | Interface | Power |")
print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|:---:|")
for _, c in cameras:
    res = f"{c.resolution_width} × {c.resolution_height}" if c.resolution_width else "---"
    print(f"| **{c.name}** | {res} | {q(c.frame_rate, 'Hz', 0)} | {c.shutter_type or '---'} | "
          f"{q(c.exposure_time, 'ms')} | {q(c.readout_time, 'ms')} | {c.interface or '---'} | {q(c.nominal_power, 'W')} |")

print("\n### LiDAR\n")
print("| Sensor | Channels | Scan rate | Max range | Range accuracy | Interface | Power |")
print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|:---:|")
for _, s in entries(Sensors.LiDAR):
    print(f"| **{s.name}** | {s.channels or '---'} | {q(s.scan_rate, 'Hz', 0)} | {q(s.max_range, 'm', 0)} | "
          f"{q(s.range_accuracy, 'mm', 0)} | {s.interface or '---'} | {q(s.nominal_power, 'W')} |")

print("\n### Inertial measurement units\n")
print("| Sensor | DoF | Sample rate | Gyro noise density | Accel noise density | Interface |")
print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|")
for _, s in entries(Sensors.IMU):
    gyro = f"{s.gyro_noise_density:~P}" if s.gyro_noise_density is not None else "---"
    accel = f"{s.accel_noise_density:~P}" if s.accel_noise_density is not None else "---"
    print(f"| **{s.name}** | {s.dofs or '---'} | {q(s.sample_rate, 'Hz', 0)} | {gyro} | {accel} | {s.interface or '---'} |")

print("\n### Safety laser scanners\n")
print("| Sensor | Protective field | Response time | Scan angle | IEC 61496 | Performance level |")
print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---|:---|")
for _, s in entries(Sensors.SafetyScanner):
    print(f"| **{s.name}** | {q(s.protective_field_range, 'm')} | {q(s.response_time, 'ms', 0)} | "
          f"{q(s.scan_angle, 'degree', 0)} | {s.iec61496_type or '---'} | {s.performance_level or '---'} |")
print()
```

## Where these numbers are used

Sensor timing sets the floor on how stale an observation is by the time the system acts on it. The
Volume IV chapters use these entries for information-age budgets (half the exposure plus readout,
transport, and processing) and for multi-camera ingestion bandwidth. The underlying formulas are in
[`physics.robotics.perception`](../api/physics.robotics.perception.qmd).
